summary: Sales request: pre-approved order form language for Dedicated throughput guarantees (tiers) + linkable definition
description:
Requester: Stephanie Nguyen (Sales Enablement)
Team: Sales (NA), with input from Jordan Blake (GTM)
Routed to: Product (Dedicated) + Legal

Context
Sales is drafting order forms / order form exhibits for Dedicated deals and needs a short, pre-approved clause describing the throughput guarantee and how it is measured, to avoid ad-hoc edits and reduce legal cycle time. Multiple deals in pipeline are asking “tokens/sec guaranteed” and requesting the exact language for the Order Form / SLA exhibit.

What Sales needs
1) A copy/pasteable clause for the Order Form that:
   - References the official measurement methodology (without embedding overly technical details in the Order Form)
   - Clarifies tier-specific commitment is defined in an attached exhibit / service schedule (tier matrix)
   - States what happens when customer exceeds assumptions (throttling vs breach)
   - Includes standard carve-outs (maintenance, customer misconfiguration, force majeure, etc.)
2) Guidance on what Sales is allowed to say in email / proposals (non-binding vs binding).
3) A “no surprises” rule for exceptions (who approves and how to document).

Constraints / notes
- Throughput varies by model + context length distribution + streaming; commitments must be tied to a defined workload profile and measurement window.
- Dedicated tier program is in beta; language should work now but not lock us into non-operationally enforceable promises.
- We want a consistent definition across: sales proposals, order forms, and SRE reporting.

Deliverable requested in this ticket
- Provide Legal-approved ‘Order Form Throughput Commitment’ clause + short fallback language for proposals.
- Provide a link to canonical docs (Confluence) for measurement methodology and tier definitions.

Due date / urgency
- P2. Needed for two active opportunities (one in procurement). Requested by end of week to unblock redlines.

Attachments / references
- Customer-side confusion theme captured in SUP-4877 (measurement for mixed prompt sizes).
- Internal project: “Dedicated throughput SLO + tier definitions” (Product DRI: Lauren Bishop).
comments:
2025-02-10 10:14 PT — Stephanie Nguyen (Reporter)
We’re getting repeated requests for “pre-approved language” we can paste into order forms. Right now AEs are paraphrasing and Legal is re-litigating definitions each time. Can we standardize a short clause that points to the measurement standard + tier exhibit? Ideally something we can put under “Service Levels / Throughput Commitment” in the Order Form.

Immediate need: one deal in procurement wants the clause this week; they are pushing for a hard tokens/sec guarantee without exclusions.

2025-02-10 12:02 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Readiness)
Routing to Product + Legal. This is also showing up in Support tickets as “what does guaranteed throughput mean?” (see SUP-4877). Suggest we anchor to the same definition Support will use when triaging throughput complaints.

2025-02-10 13:25 PT — Lauren Bishop (Product DRI, Dedicated)
Agree on standard language. For consistency, Order Form should reference (1) Dedicated tier definitions page and (2) Throughput Measurement Standard. We should explicitly say we will throttle when customers exceed tier assumptions (concurrency / max input lengths), and that throttling is expected behavior, not an SLO breach.

Michael/Sofia (Legal): can you help craft a clause that’s short but defensible? We can provide the tier exhibit table separately (Standard/Performance/Premium + workload profile).

2025-02-11 09:08 PT — Michael Grant (Assignee, Legal)
Acknowledged. Drafting “Throughput Commitment” clause with (a) defined term for Throughput, (b) reference to “Throughput Measurement Standard” (incorporated by reference), and (c) remedies only as specified in the SLA / service credits section.

Open question: do we want to put the actual numeric commitment in the Order Form (tokens/sec) or only via an attached Exhibit A (Tier Schedule)? My recommendation: keep numeric values in the Exhibit so we can update tier matrices without reworking boilerplate language.

2025-02-11 11:47 PT — Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel)
+1 to keeping numeric values in the Exhibit.

Also recommend we avoid “guarantee” in the Order Form header and use “Service Level Objective” or “Throughput Commitment,” then define the credit remedy (if any) in the MSA/SLA addendum. If Sales must say “guarantee,” ensure it’s tied to the credit language and carve-outs.

I’ll propose language with:
- “Successful Requests” definition (exclude 4xx, customer-side disconnects)
- Maintenance exclusions
- Overload/backpressure behavior (throttling) called out as non-breach when customer exceeds assumptions.

2025-02-12 16:22 PT — Lauren Bishop (Product)
Product preference:
- Use primary metric: sustained output tokens/sec at deployment level, measured as rate over rolling window, aggregated per tier per month for reporting.
- Make it clear that mixed prompt sizes are supported but commitments assume a declared “Workload Profile” (prompt length distribution + max context) in Exhibit.

We can provide Sales with a “proposal safe” one-liner: “Dedicated tiers include a defined throughput commitment measured per Redwood’s published measurement standard, with customer-visible reporting.”

2025-02-14 10:05 PT — Michael Grant (Legal)
Proposed pre-approved Order Form clause (v1) below. Please confirm Product/SRE are comfortable with the operational semantics.

---
Order Form / Exhibit Language — Throughput Commitment (Pre-Approved)
“Throughput Commitment. For Customer’s Redwood Dedicated deployment(s) identified in this Order Form (each, a ‘Dedicated Deployment’), Redwood will provide the throughput service level objective set forth in the applicable Service Schedule / Exhibit (the ‘Throughput Commitment’) for the applicable Tier and Workload Profile. ‘Throughput’ will be measured as Sustained Output Tokens per Second for Successful Requests, calculated and reported in accordance with Redwood’s then-current Throughput Measurement Standard (available at: [internal link to be replaced with customer-facing URL at launch]) (the ‘Measurement Standard’). If Customer’s usage exceeds the Tier’s documented assumptions (including concurrency, request rate, or maximum context / token limits), Redwood may apply admission control, queueing, or throttling to protect service stability; such throttling is expected behavior and will not be considered a failure to meet the Throughput Commitment. The Throughput Commitment does not apply during Excluded Events as defined in the Measurement Standard (including scheduled maintenance, emergency maintenance, Customer-caused errors, Customer network issues, or force majeure). Remedies, if any, for failure to meet the Throughput Commitment are limited to those expressly set forth in the applicable SLA / service credits addendum.”
---

Notes:
- We should swap the Measurement Standard link to a customer-facing doc before external use.
- Exhibit must define: Tier, region, model(s) (or model family), Workload Profile (prompt distribution + max context), and the numeric throughput target.

Stephanie/Jordan: can you confirm if Sales needs a shorter “proposal snippet” too?

2025-02-14 12:18 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
SRE review: language is consistent with how we plan to alert/track. Specifically like the explicit callout that throttling when exceeding assumptions is not an SLO breach.

Request: ensure “Successful Requests” definition aligns to Measurement Standard (exclude client disconnects and 4xx; include 5xx as service failures). Also: specify measurement window is defined in the Measurement Standard (so we can change rolling window without re-papering contracts).

2025-02-14 13:40 PT — Stephanie Nguyen (Sales Enablement)
Yes, please provide a proposal-safe snippet we can put in email / quotes that’s non-binding unless in the Order Form. Also: can we have a one-sentence answer for “Is it tokens/sec guaranteed?”

We can live with ‘Throughput Commitment’ term; AEs will still say ‘guarantee’ verbally, but we can coach them to map it to the commitment + credit remedy.

2025-02-15 09:22 PT — Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel)
Proposal snippet (pre-approved, non-binding unless included in signed Order Form):
“Redwood Dedicated tiers include a defined throughput commitment (e.g., sustained tokens/sec under an agreed workload profile), measured and reported per Redwood’s published Throughput Measurement Standard. Final commitments, assumptions, and remedies (if any) are set forth in the Order Form and applicable SLA addendum.”

One-sentence answer to ‘Is it tokens/sec guaranteed?’
“Yes—Dedicated includes a throughput commitment (measured as sustained output tokens/sec for successful requests) under documented workload assumptions; if you exceed those assumptions, the platform may throttle to protect stability.”

Reminder: do not attach internal Confluence links externally; use customer-facing doc once published.

2025-02-18 16:05 PT — Michael Grant (Legal) — Resolution
Finalized + approved language for Sales to use:
1) Order Form clause: “Throughput Commitment” (as posted in the 2025-02-14 draft, with SRE edits: ‘Successful Requests’ + measurement window explicitly controlled by Measurement Standard).
2) Proposal/email snippet: approved (see 2025-02-15 comment).

Action items
- Product (Lauren) to provide customer-facing URL for Measurement Standard + Tier Definitions prior to external distribution.
- Sales Enablement (Stephanie) to update templates: Order Form Exhibit (Tier/Workload Profile) + internal playbook for handling ‘exception asks’ (route via Product + Legal).

Marking Resolved; reopen if external doc link changes or we need to update carve-outs post-beta.
resolution: Provided Legal-approved, copy/pasteable Order Form clause for Dedicated Throughput Commitment (tier + workload profile based), plus a proposal-safe non-binding snippet and a one-sentence FAQ answer. Confirmed alignment with SRE semantics (throttling when exceeding assumptions is not an SLO breach) and that details (measurement window/exclusions) are governed by the Throughput Measurement Standard. Sales Enablement to update templates; Product to publish customer-facing doc URLs.
